_note: Whole-house gauntlet status. Update state/round/note/render per room as critics report, then run: python -m roomkit.house_progress
headline: The outside of the house, and the four rooms nobody had judged
lede: Every room of this house is being rebuilt as procedural 3D geometry inside the live Home Assistant app, then screenshotted from the same spot the reference photo was taken. A separate critic with fresh context puts the two side by side, blind, and says which is which. If ours is obvious, it goes back to the builder. This run covers the five spaces the owner photographed last: the front and back of the house, the garage, the movie room and the arcade.
stamp: v3 run · 23 Aug 2026 · all five built, all four critics lost to a session limit — nothing here has been judged yet
hero_label: Every room in the house furnished. 241 pieces, all 423 Home Assistant device markers intact.

rooms.name: Frontyard
rooms.note: The front beds were being sited off the roof outline rather than the real walls, so the whole planting bed stood four to five feet out on the lawn, and the wheeled bin was inside the garage. Everything is now anchored to landmarks raycast off the shell itself: the driveway is a poured slab with real control joints, a dry-stacked slate course retains the pad, and the beds, flagstone, boxwood and lamp post sit where the photograph puts them. The concrete matches the photo on value, spread and fine-scale gradient. No lights: the photographs are dusk shots and the owner has held those back.

rooms.name: Backyard
rooms.note: The emptiest space in the project, and it was worse than empty — the entire back yard was rendering as the shell's bare white site pad. It now has the deck the photographs show, built against the real rear wall with its rail, steps, grill, closed parasol and wicker seating, over a lawn edged with rock borders, stepping stones, free-standing clipped mounds and a treeline moved out to the lot lines. The shell's own patio set was hidden; its baked open parasol had to be cut out of the 79,000-triangle mesh it was merged into, along with the SketchUp edge overlay that kept drawing its ribs in mid-air.

rooms.name: Garage
rooms.note: Had no reference photo at all before this run, and its contents had been inferred rather than observed — the photographs contradicted most of them, so fourteen invented pieces were replaced with what is actually there: the black coin-tile floor, the printed banner, grey metal cabinets, the wreathed service door up two steps. The wall spread came down from 91.5 to 13.0 after the builder found the previous fit had been measuring the neighbouring rooms' walls, which push a third of a foot through into this one.

rooms.name: Movie Room
rooms.note: Rebuilt for a footprint that had been re-traced 3.4 ft wider since the last pass, which had left its ceiling, crown, baseboards and chair rail all stopping short of the east wall. It also settled a long-standing puzzle: the north wall's 'clipping' was never a tone-curve problem, it was the Arcade Room's wall standing a third of a foot inside this room. A skin authored clear of it fixed the wall outright and gave the chair rail a step that had never rendered.

rooms.name: Arcade Room
rooms.note: Was 180 degrees out: the arcade cabinets had been built along the west wall and they are on the east. That is the seventh room in this project to ship a structural orientation error, and it was caught by registering the basement plan against the stairwell row and the doorway it shares with the Movie Room. Rebuilt from the corrected orientation, its four walls now sit within 11 bytes of each other — the tightest in the house.

rooms.name: Master Bedroom
rooms.note: The bed is a KING. Round 3 had 'proved' a queen from photo anchors and that was carried for three rounds; the measurement had been taken against a headboard 25 degrees off square, foreshortened by a quarter. Re-measured against objects at the same depth, the shams are 36-inch king pillows. The invented white chest was deleted for the armchair the photo and plan both show, a TV added, soft surfaces given real texture, and the room slimmed from 3.41 MB to 1.74 MB. It also found a bug in the shared GLB library and independently confirmed the entry vestibule was misplaced.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.note: Round 3 failed on two counts and round 4 has closed one of them outright: the room is down from 5.88 MB to 1.66 MB — 27 percent of the whole house to under 9 — with no content removed, by taking the fine gradient from a tiled texture instead of the mesh. The rug was then re-derived rather than guessed: a floor-facing surface here renders at 0.89 times albedo plus 55.3, so the weave was re-based to hit photo F's own mean and spread, and the island's contact shadow was moved onto the counter footprint it actually sits under. What remains from the critic is the counter stone, still marks rather than a field at high-pass energy 0.25 against the photograph's 0.40 to 0.48.

rooms.name: Living Room
rooms.note: Round 4 failed on the flaw at the centre of the whole loop: standard deviation is scale-blind, so every fabric and masonry surface matched the photograph's sd while being 3 to 7 times too smooth at the scale a person actually sees. Round 5 is answering it with texture rather than geometry, which also bought the payload back — 1.98 MB to 1.64 with the mesh cells 30 percent coarser and the metrics re-measured after the change instead of assumed. Two long-standing defects went with it: the contact shadows now read the live object positions out of the running app, so they can no longer drift off the furniture they belong to as they had after round 5 moved nearly every seat, and the three outdoor view boards were re-cut to sit behind their openings rather than standing in the yard outside the shell. The per-wall albedo skins — the unpulled lever, wall spread 114 — are what is left before it can be judged.

rooms.name: Dining
rooms.note: Rebuilt into the re-traced polygon. Verified orientation three independent ways and confirmed round 1 had it right. The bay is real now, so its three windows sit on the actual canted facets as cut holes, and both doorways are true passages — and it registered the kitchen doorway to the exact world span room 6 had already cut on its own side, so the two rooms' holes align instead of each showing the other's jamb. The 7.8 ft table fits without being shrunk: at that size the west end chair sits in the bay mouth exactly where the photo puts it.

rooms.name: Rios Room
rooms.note: Round 2 found the room was 180 degrees out, not merely too big: re-deriving orientation from the floor plan against two adjacencies puts the windows on the SOUTH wall. It also found there are two rubber trees, one at each end of the window wall, which is why round 1's corner never resolved. Windows rebuilt to 4.85 ft tall with a 1 ft header as measured, cut as real openings; the room-filling emissive wall wash deleted rather than re-tuned, and the room now meters within a few points of an empty room of the same size — it is no longer compensating for the renderer.

rooms.name: Office
rooms.note: The first room built with per-wall albedo skins, and they closed the problem every previous critic named: the four walls went from N 234 / W 210 / E 171 / S 149, a spread of 85.5, down to a spread of 22.9 — real rooms sit within about 30. Its orientation check against the floor plan also caught two errors the shell pass had made: only one window where there are two, and an invented door on the west wall that is actually the bathroom party wall.

rooms.name: Guest Room
rooms.note: The sixth room whose orientation turned out wrong: the shell pass had it 180 degrees out on Z, with the headboard, closet and dresser all on the wrong walls. Proved three ways — registering the plan to world coordinates and sampling the bed and pillow icons, a camera solve from seven identifiable points at rms 1.16 degrees (the rival positions score 18.3), and the round mirror, which reflects the blinded window and a picture and therefore faces west. Payload 0.563 MB, the lightest furnished room in the house.

rooms.name: Master Bathroom
rooms.note: Finished. Both vanity mirrors reflect two different windows, which is what fixes the room's orientation — a mirror cannot reflect the wall it hangs on. Marble veins rebuilt as thin wandering lines where they had been axis-aligned blocks that read as static.

rooms.name: Second-floor bathroom
rooms.note: The shell pass had this room wrong twice: the door was at the east end of the north wall, where standing in the doorway would put you inside the shower, and the toilet was on the wrong side of the window. A framed print visible on the south wall THROUGH the shower glass is only possible with the shower between the door and the corner.

rooms.name: First-floor bathroom
rooms.note: The shell pass recorded a door on the west wall, which is the Living Room party wall. The plan's only gap is on the south. Vanity values were solved from photo ratios rather than hex codes, because a GLB collects roughly twice what a wall does and the first grey cabinet rendered brighter than the wall behind it.

rooms.name: First-floor hallway & stairs
rooms.note: Front door with sidelights, staircase with runner and black rail. Its four contact shadows were sitting below the slab's polygon offset, invisible; raised and strengthened.

rooms.name: Second-floor hallway
rooms.note: Round 2, rebuilding against six new owner photos. The stairwell is now a REAL hole in the slab -- the footprint became an L and the flight below shows through, which round 1 could only fake with a painted panel. Doors, stair dressing and soft goods in build.

rooms.name: Master Closet
rooms.ref: C:\Users\Manuel\Desktop\Pro\3d HA\docs\photos-jpg\Walk in the closet to Master Bedroom.jpg
rooms.note: The shell pass had the ceiling rake and black accent wall on the east wall. Raycasting the house-shell GLB from above showed the roof underside constant in x and falling in z — a 6:12 pitch dropping south — so both belong on the south wall.

rooms.name: Laundry
rooms.note: Structural correction: the shell pass had put the washer and dryer at the west end of the north wall, which is exactly where the plan puts the step and door in from the garage. Moved east to the plan's own appliance icon. Honest caveat recorded: the traced footprint merges the real mudroom and laundry alcove, so no camera inside it can reproduce the photo — the side-by-side is a content match, not a geometry match. Spread 89.6 to 18.2.

rooms.name: Pantry
rooms.note: Both photographs show the doors closed, so the entire interior is inferred: five-tier shelving on the wall you face through the doors, stocked, with a step stool. Only one wall yields a clean metering field, so the skins were sized from the laundry's set scaled by the two rooms' bare west walls, which agree to 3 percent.

facts.Geometry: re-traced from the three floor plans through one cross-registered transform; the old trace was ~28% too large linearly
facts.Accuracy bar: the photograph of each actual room
facts.Device markers: 423, every one still live and controllable
facts.Wall-light spread: 222-125 bytes -> 238-158 after the app-level lighting fix
facts.First floor: ~1,250 sq ft living + 443 sq ft garage
facts.Payload: 18.9 MB across 241 pieces; budget 1.5 MB/room and 300 KB/piece
facts.Wall spread: 91 down to 12-23 bytes per room via per-wall albedo
